feedback.problem:
In **ascending order,** the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}=1$ intersects the line $y=x$ are

$\,x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=x,$ we first replace $y$ with $x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{12{x}^{2}}{36}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{9{x}^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =4 \\ x & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection are
$x=-2$ and $x=2.$
